description: Deterministic multi-domain natural-language seeds for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next PLE/MoE trace characterization. These prompts are benchmark material, not quality-evaluation questions.
request_seeds: Analyze how a memory hierarchy should prioritize data when fast capacity is scarce and access frequency changes over time.
Explain how to debug a concurrent software service when latency spikes appear only under sustained request traffic.
Compare two computer architecture designs that trade local capacity for lower data-movement cost during inference.
Develop a careful experimental plan for separating causal performance effects from measurement and instrumentation overhead.
Reason about an algorithm that maintains a bounded cache while requests repeatedly revisit a changing subset of objects.
Describe how an engineer should validate a hardware-software interface before drawing conclusions from end-to-end benchmarks.
Assess a scientific hypothesis in which a large conditional memory competes with sparse model parameters for host capacity.
Explain the difference between temporal locality, frequency skew, working-set size, and cache hit rate using precise examples.
Design a reproducible data-analysis workflow that preserves raw observations and makes every transformation independently auditable.
Discuss how queueing, overlap, and resource contention can change observed service time without changing the underlying algorithm.
Solve a planning problem where several tasks share limited memory, storage bandwidth, and accelerator time under fixed constraints.
Review a hypothetical systems paper and identify which claims require direct measurement rather than projection or literature evidence.
Explain how sparse expert routing can create nonuniform memory demand across layers and across successive generated tokens.
Analyze when prefetching helps a conditional lookup workload and when inaccurate prediction can waste bandwidth or cache capacity.
Describe a method for comparing two memory placements while keeping model revision, workload, runtime, and hardware unchanged.
Reason about the consequences of moving a large read-mostly table from host memory to a slower but higher-capacity tier.
Explain how deterministic traces can be used to screen design points without treating projected latency as measured performance.
Develop a debugging strategy for a GPU application that combines host-side offload, asynchronous transfers, and dynamic caching.
Analyze how input length can change prefill behavior, decode behavior, sparse routing, and conditional-memory reuse in a language model.
Summarize the evidence needed to decide whether reclaiming host memory for experts produces a meaningful end-to-end inference benefit.
continuation_sentences: A useful measurement separates the identity of an accessed object from the time required to obtain it.
Repeated accesses can arise within one request or across independent requests, and those cases should be reported separately.
A bounded cache exposes both compulsory misses and capacity misses as the active working set evolves.
The same aggregate hit rate can hide very different reuse-distance distributions and therefore different scaling behavior.
Host memory is finite, so reserving capacity for one structure necessarily changes the capacity available to another structure.
Storage traffic should be counted from explicit transfers or block activity rather than inferred from accelerator utilization.
Instrumentation is allowed to perturb a trace run, but a perturbed trace run must not be reused as a throughput benchmark.
Every promoted measurement should record the exact model revision, runtime revision, repository state, and workload definition.
A projection can identify promising capacity points while remaining insufficient to establish an end-to-end performance claim.
Request-level correlation requires timestamps that share a clock domain and intervals that do not overlap ambiguously.
Concurrency changes service overlap and queueing, so aggregate concurrent traces require different semantics from sequential traces.
Longer inputs can expose a larger prefill working set even when the decode path activates a similar number of experts per token.
Sparse routing reduces compute activation but can increase irregular data movement when selected experts are not resident.
A popularity distribution is useful for static placement, whereas reuse distance is directly connected to replacement-cache behavior.
Cold capacity can be large without being useful if its access latency cannot be hidden by computation or accurate prefetching.
A causal comparison changes one placement decision while keeping endpoint configuration and workload constant.
Independent repetitions are needed because operating-system activity, storage state, and runtime warmup can affect observed latency.
Fail-closed processing is preferable when a missing identifier could silently assign an event to the wrong request.
Raw traces should remain immutable so later analyses can be regenerated when metrics or statistical methods change.
A model-specific characterization should not be generalized to other architectures without evidence that their routing and lookup behavior match.
The prefill phase processes many input positions together, whereas decode repeatedly advances the sequence by a small number of positions.
Working-set curves reveal how much capacity is needed before additional memory produces diminishing locality benefits.
Transfer bytes per token connect routing behavior to memory-system demand more directly than a count of selected experts alone.
If a large table is externalized, the reclaimed host capacity can increase expert residency only when the memory budget is actually binding.
A capacity model should make its accounting boundary explicit instead of mixing application allocations with unrelated system memory.
Exact prompt token counts remove one source of variation when comparing traces across input-length conditions.
Deterministic request material allows a failed experiment to be repeated without changing the access sequence by accident.
Different semantic topics can exercise different token sequences and routing choices even when their rendered lengths are identical.
A complete campaign should detect missing cases, duplicate cases, changed artifacts, and provenance drift before aggregation.
Container image identity matters because a mutable tag alone is insufficient to prove that two experiments used identical runtime bits.
An explicit server-log window helps distinguish errors that happened during a case from warnings produced during model startup.
Kernel compilation during a trace run may change timing while leaving the observed object sequence useful for locality analysis.
Out-of-memory errors and runtime exceptions invalidate a trace case because they can truncate or distort the observed access stream.
A consistent expert slot size can be derived when explicit transfer bytes are divisible by the number of transferred experts.
A consistent PLE footprint can be derived from measured row width and versioned table geometry without guessing the storage format.
Manual byte-size overrides are useful for diagnostics but should be labeled so they cannot be confused with measured inputs.
The useful counterfactual is not infinite memory but the number of additional experts that fit inside the reclaimed capacity.
Screening should prioritize budgets where externalization changes predicted traffic enough to justify expensive measured comparisons.
A negative result remains scientifically useful when the predeclared gate is evaluated without changing thresholds after observing the data.
The final motivation claim requires non-trace measurements because instrumentation overhead can otherwise become part of the apparent benefit.
